release_notes.en-US: Adds controls to the toolbar popup for turning link scanning on or off and managing custom link rules. Add an exact URL to Don't flag to suppress a known false positive, or to Always flag to mark a known false negative for review. Rules and the switch are stored locally in Firefox extension storage; link analysis remains on-device with no remote requests or data collection.

version.approval_notes:
Version 0.2.0 adds user-controlled settings to the toolbar popup: a master scanning switch, an exact-URL Don't flag list for known false positives, and an exact-URL Always flag list for known false negatives. Each saved URL is canonicalized with the browser URL parser, restricted to HTTP or HTTPS, and matched exactly after its fragment is removed. Duplicate values are collapsed. If a user adds the same URL to the opposite list, the previous rule is removed so the outcome cannot be ambiguous.

The new storage permission is used only for browser.storage.local to retain these settings across sessions. content.js loads the settings before its first scan, watches local setting changes in every injected frame, and clears existing annotations immediately when scanning is disabled or a false-positive rule is added. A false-negative match receives the local reason 'manually flagged link'. No URLs or settings leave the browser.

There are no remote requests, telemetry, external services, remotely hosted code, or changes to declared data collection, which remains none. Host permissions are unchanged. The repository test suite covers the storage permission and packaged helper, exact URL and fragment behavior, false-positive suppression, false-negative marking, disabled scanning, and both Firefox Promise-based and Chromium callback-based popup messaging. Mozilla lint and the unsigned package build are run before submission.
